title: Discriminant validity: HTMT and HTMT2
summary: Discriminant validity asks whether constructs are empirically distinct; the HTMT ratio estimates their correlation and the Fornell–Larcker criterion often misses problems.

body.text: Two constructs measured as distinct must not be empirically the same. The [[htmt]] estimates the correlation between two reflective constructs from the indicator correlations (Henseler et al. 2015).

body.display: HTMTᵢⱼ = r̄(between i and j) / √( r̄(within i) · r̄(within j) )
body.explanation: r̄(between) is the mean correlation of indicators of construct i with indicators of j; r̄(within) is the mean correlation among the indicators of one construct. [[htmt2]] uses geometric instead of arithmetic means, which is more robust when loadings differ (Roemer et al. 2021).

body.caption: Raise the between-construct correlations and watch HTMT approach 1.

body.text: Henseler et al. (2015) suggest flagging HTMT above .85 for conceptually distinct constructs, or above .90 for conceptually similar ones; a stronger version tests whether HTMT is significantly below the threshold. SEM Studio currently reports point values of HTMT and HTMT2. The [[fornell-larcker]] criterion (AVE greater than the squared construct correlation) performs poorly at detecting problems (Henseler et al. 2015). In the poor-discriminant data HTMT(A, B) is .973, yet Fornell–Larcker passes by a hair: AVE(A) = .719 against a squared correlation of .716.

mistake.title: Deleting items until HTMT passes
mistake.text: Removing indicators to push HTMT under .85 changes the constructs and capitalises on chance. Ask first whether the constructs are conceptually distinct, examine item wording and [[cross-loadings]], and consider whether theory allows treating them as one construct.

tryIt.task: Run PLS-SEM on the poor-discriminant data. Read HTMT and HTMT2 for A and B, then the Fornell–Larcker table. Which criterion flags the problem?

checks.question: HTMT(A, B) = .97 while Fornell–Larcker is satisfied for A and B. What do you conclude?

options.text: Discriminant validity of A and B is doubtful; Fornell–Larcker is known to miss such cases.
options.feedback: Correct. HTMT near 1 means A and B are nearly the same empirically.

options.text: Discriminant validity holds because one criterion is met.
options.feedback: Fornell–Larcker has low sensitivity; a passing value does not outweigh an HTMT of .97.

options.text: HTMT is not valid when loadings are high.
options.feedback: High loadings make HTMT a good estimate of the construct correlation, not a worse one.

options.text: The correlation between two reflective constructs, from their indicators.
options.feedback: Correct, under the assumption of equal loadings within each construct (HTMT2 relaxes it).
Reliability is a within-construct property; HTMT is a between-construct ratio.

options.text: The path coefficient between the two constructs.
options.feedback: A path is a directed, partial effect; HTMT is a symmetric correlation estimate.
